summary: Lehner's excavation of the Heit el-Ghurab 'workers town' found long galleries/barracks that he hypothesizes housed a rotating labor force of ~1,600-2,000 workers, fed well (young male cattle, bread, beer).
content: We now see the enigmatic rows of long galleries... as barracks housing for a rotating labor force, perhaps as large as 1,600 to 2,000 workers... There are scores of bakeries flanking the galleries, as well as an abundance of bone... [Redding] could identify much of it as 'young, under two years of age, and it tended to be male.' Here was evidence of many people... feasting on prime beef.
